title: Elodie and the Oath
premise: Ansel Thackeray survives in the memoryless valley by stealing recollections from travelers and selling them back, a trade that keeps them fed and forgotten. When a mute child arrives speaking the dead tongue of the First Kingdoms, Ansel learns the valley's magiclessness is not sanctuary but a cage built by the Oath—a bargain their own stolen memories once sealed. To free King Aldric from the crown-thing that devours him and the child who carries the unbinding word, Ansel must leave the valley, surrender every memory they have hoarded, and choose between loyalty to the mentor who made them a thief and the truth that their survival cost a kingdom its king. In the end, Ansel breaks the Oath at the price of forgetting themselves entirely; the child, remembering for both of them, becomes the new keeper of what was lost.
about_author: Gideon Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging letters no one claimed. They write fantasy about the things people bury to keep living.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet the valley where magic cannot follow and Ansel's trade: lifting memories from travelers and selling them back at the border. Emotional beat: wary contentment masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Price in Small Coins
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A routine theft goes wrong when a merchant recognizes his own sold-back grief. Ansel pockets a memory he should return. Beat: first crack in the moral armor.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. During a storm, a mute child appears at Ansel's cottage, speaking a language older than any kingdom—and the words make the valley's stones hum. Beat: dread and wonder entwined.

chapters.title: What the Stones Remember
chapters.summary: Child's POV (rendered through sensation). The child, Wren, perceives the valley as a wound in the world and Ansel as someone stitched into it. Beat: alien tenderness.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Corvane, the fence who taught Ansel the trade, arrives demanding the child be handed over. His ledger lists names Ansel doesn't remember giving. Beat: unease.

chapters.title: Sold Back My Own Name
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Examining their oldest stolen memory, Ansel finds a gap shaped exactly like themselves. Beat: vertigo—the thief discovers they were robbed first.

chapters.title: The Word Beneath the Tongue
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren teaches Ansel three syllables of the old language; each one burns a hole in the valley's silence. Beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Corvane offers protection, food, a future—if Ansel surrenders Wren. He reminds Ansel of debts Ansel can't verify. Beat: loyalty tested against instinct.

chapters.title: Night of the Humming Road
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ansel and Wren flee north along a road that remembers travelers' footsteps. Corvane's hunters follow. Beat: terror laced with exhilaration.

chapters.title: First Magic
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Outside the valley, Wren's speech kindles small wonders—light in cupped hands. Ansel watches, unable to touch it. Beat: longing and grief for a self they never had.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A ferryman demands payment in memory. Ansel pays with a stranger's joy and feels it hollow them. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Crowned City
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They reach Aldermont, where King Aldric parades in glass-eyed splendor while his shadow moves a half-second late. Beat: horror dressed in pageantry.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing Him
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren sees the crown-thing clearly: an oath given flesh, feeding on the king's consent. Beat: pity for the monster's host.

chapters.title: A Thief Among Courtiers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Disguised as a memory-broker, Ansel infiltrates the palace and steals a courtier's recollection of the coronation. Beat: competence as camouflage.

chapters.title: What Was Sworn at the Coronation
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The stolen memory reveals the Oath: the crown-thing saved the dying kingdom, and the price was renewed every seven years—in children. Beat: revulsion.

chapters.title: Wren Is the Tithe
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel realizes Wren fled the palace; the child is this year's payment, carrying the unbinding word no one dares speak. Beat: protective fury.

chapters.title: The Queen Who Isn't
chapters.summary: Queen Maren's POV. Maren knows what wears her husband's face and has kept the peace by pretending. She catches Ansel. Beat: complicity and exhaustion.

chapters.title: Bargain in the Dark Gallery
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren offers Ansel the king's private records in exchange for one condition: Aldric must never learn what she allowed. Beat: loyalty vs. truth sharpened.

chapters.title: The King's Forgotten Hours
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Reading Aldric's sealed journals, Ansel finds the king has been writing pleas inside his own memories, begging whoever reads to break the Oath. Beat: heartbreak.

chapters.title: Corvane Comes to Court
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Corvane arrives as the crown-thing's broker, revealing he has sold tithe-children for decades—including, long ago, someone from the valley. Beat: betrayal confirmed.

chapters.title: The Memory I Sold
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel confronts Corvane and learns the truth: Ansel was a tithe-child who escaped, and Corvane erased the memory to keep them useful. Beat: identity shattered.

chapters.title: Running on Borrowed Ground
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hunted through the city's undercrofts, Wren uses the old language to bend stone, each word costing years of their own memory. Beat: sacrifice escalating.

chapters.title: Maren's Choice
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The crown-thing suspects Maren's treachery and offers her Aldric's life if she delivers the child. Beat: the corrupting arithmetic of power.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Word
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Wren, half-erased, finally gives Ansel the full unbinding—but it can only be spoken by someone holding the Oath's original memory, which lies in the valley. Beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: Return to the Cage
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel and Wren slip back into the magicless valley, pursued. Home feels smaller now. Beat: bittersweet homecoming.

chapters.title: Corvane's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Corvane corners them at the cottage; Ansel defeats him not with violence but by returning every memory he ever sold, drowning him in his own conscience. Beat: mercy as weapon.

chapters.title: The Hoard Opened
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel opens their hidden cache of stolen memories and searches for the Oath's origin—finding instead their own childhood, the night they escaped the tithe. Beat: devastating recognition.

chapters.title: I Was There
chapters.summary: Child-Ansel's POV (memory sequence). Seven-year-old Ansel watched the first unbinding attempted and failed; their mother spoke the word and was unmade. Beat: inherited courage.

chapters.title: The Mother's Syllable
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Within the recovered memory, Ansel's mother hid the true unbinding inside her final word to her child. Beat: love outlasting erasure.

chapters.title: March on Aldermont
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. With Wren fading, Ansel races back to the capital as the seven-year renewal begins and children are gathered in the square. Beat: desperate urgency.

chapters.title: The Renewal
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren watches the tithe begin and finally breaks, ordering the guards to stand down. Beat: redemption bought at the brink.

chapters.title: Storming the Crown Room
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel fights through the crown-thing's bound servants to reach Aldric, who barely remembers his own name. Beat: climax begins.

chapters.title: The King Remembers
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Ansel returns the king's sealed journals as living memory; Aldric reclaims himself long enough to consent to his own unbinding. Beat: agency restored.

chapters.title: Speak It
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The crown-thing offers Ansel everything—safety, the valley, Wren whole—if they stay silent. Beat: temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: The Word and the Cost
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel speaks the unbinding. The Oath demands a life of memory in exchange; Ansel gives all of theirs. Beat: climax—the price paid in full.

chapters.title: Unmade, Unbound
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The crown-thing unravels; Aldric collapses human and weeping. Ansel stands blank-eyed, knowing no one, including themselves. Beat: triumph shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: The Keeper of What Was Lost
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, remembering everything for both of them, chooses to stay beside Ansel rather than return to the old ways. Beat: devotion without debt.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Relearning Its Name
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Aldric abolishes the tithe and builds a house of returned memories; Maren stays, honestly now. Beat: repair beginning.

chapters.title: Teaching the Thief Their Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren tells Ansel who they were, story by story, and Ansel decides which parts to believe. Beat: gentle reconstruction of a self.

chapters.title: Elodie
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Wren reveals Ansel's true name—Elodie—and Elodie chooses to keep it, walking out of the valley not to hide but to begin. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
